name: What is the difference between an ADU and a JADU (Junior Accessory Dwelling Unit)?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between an ADU and a JADU (Junior Accessory Dwelling Unit)?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Junior Accessory Dwelling Unit (JADU) is a specific type of ADU that is no more than 500 square feet and is created within the existing walls of a single-family home. It must include an efficiency kitchen and typically requires a separate exterior entrance, but may share a bathroom with the main dwelling. Unlike a full ADU, a JADU can only be built within an existing or proposed single-family structure. Both offer housing solutions, but JADUs have stricter size and location requirements.
acceptedAnswer.description: A JADU is a smaller ADU (max 500 sq ft) built within an existing single-family home, requiring an efficiency kitchen and separate entrance.
